Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: 3-year prepay with ramp / flexibility

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Lumos is excited about Redwood's latency profile and cost math. Our procurement lead asked me to confirm whether you can support a three-year prepay structure with a ramped commitment and a limited true-up window in year 3. Specifically: 
- Target: $1.2M ARR-equivalent committed spend over 36 months (paid upfront, or split annual invoices)
- Request: a term discount to reflect the multi-year prepay (we're modeling a ~25–30% total discount)
- Flexibility ask: ability to reduce committed capacity by up to 20% in year 3 without penalty if actual usage materially undershoots forecasts (we'd propose a 60-day notice)

I've attached the RFP and our traffic forecasts (Lumos_RFP_Q2.pdf). Can you send a strawman term sheet and confirm whether this is something Redwood would consider? We have a procurement window to close by end of May.

Best,
Anika
Head of Product, Lumos Analytics
Anika Shah

Hi Anika — thanks for the details and the RFP. This is definitely something we can structure, but a few clarifying q's before I pull finance/legal into a term sheet: 

- Are you looking to pay 100% upfront, or would you prefer annual invoicing (split-pay) with the same committed discount?
- For the year-3 protection, is the 20% reduction a hard cap or a part of a stepped down schedule?
- Any specific security/compliance clauses that would affect pricing (we can surface SOC2/HIPAA add-ons if needed)?

I'll draft a strawman term sheet after I confirm payment cadence and loop in my finance partner for discount authority. If you prefer, I can send a preliminary term sheet today for discussion.

Thanks — Camila

Team — forwarding Lumos' ask (attached). They want a 3-year prepay with a ramp and a potential year-3 reduction clause. Key commercial asks: ~ $1.2M total commitment; customer is modeling a 25–30% discount and wants up to 20% downward flexibility in year 3 with ~60-day notice. They need terms by EoM May.

My proposed strawman (see attached redwood_term_sheet_3yr_v1.pdf):
- 3-year committed prepay $1.2M total; paid 50% upfront / 25% at 12mo / 25% at 24mo (we can do 100% upfront if procurement prefers)
- Discount: 22% off list for the total committed amount (applied at invoice)
- Year-3 protection: one-time down-adjustment up to 15% without penalty, additional reductions up to 20% incur a pro-rated credit at the effective usage rate (60-day notice)
- True-up: 90-day true-up at the end of each 12mo period; overages billed at a blended committed rate + 10% premium
- Cap: finance wants to cap total cumulative credit liability at $120k

Asking for approvals: 
- Karthik: can finance sign off on 22% + $120k cap and the invoice schedule?
- Rachel: any legal flags on the year-3 reduction language / cap structure?

Attachments: Lumos_RFP_Q2.pdf, redwood_term_sheet_3yr_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Camila
(Account Exec)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Lumos - 3yr prepay request — need pricing approval / exceptions

Camila — reviewed the strawman. Finance can approve a max 20% discount tied to the payment schedule below, or 22% if we get 100% upfront and a hard cumulative credit cap that is sub-$100k. A few notes: 

- Preferred payment: 100% upfront improves NPV materially; if Lumos insists on split invoices we should reduce the discount to 20% for business protection.
- Credit liability: approve a $100k cap if 100% upfront; $120k cap only if we take 50/25/25.
- True-up mechanics: keep the 90-day true-up but add a cap on monthly refundable credits (e.g., no more than 25% of committed monthly run-rate per month).
- Commercial guardrail: require a quarterly usage review for visibility and a rollback clause if usage drops >40% quarter-over-quarter.

If you want to offer 22% we need an exec sign-off (Vanessa) and an email confirmation that Lumos will accept the cap and true-up mechanics in the term.

Deal ID HSB-9876 noted.
Karthik
VP, Finance (Revenue Ops)
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks team — I concur with finance's guardrails. Given Lumos' strategic fit and the velocity in our product evaluation, I'm comfortable approving a 22% discount only if: 

1) We get 100% upfront (preferred) OR 50/25/25 with the $120k cap explicitly spelled out in the term sheet.
2) We include a quarterly review cadence and a one-time performance credit (5% of committed spend) that we can apply if SLOs are missed in the first 6 months.
3) Rachel to confirm legal language for the year-3 reduction and ensure it's limited to one exercise of the reduction option per contract term.

If those are acceptable, Camila please send the revised term sheet and DocuSign link; I'll approve the envelope and expedite.

- Vanessa

Hi Anika — thanks for the patience. Per internal approvals, linked below is the final term summary and DocuSign envelope. High-level: 

- Total committed prepay: $1.2M over 36 months
- Discount: 22% off list applied to the committed spend (condition: 100% upfront payment). If you prefer split invoices (50/25/25) the discount will be 20% and the credit cap will be $120k.
- Year-3 reduction: one-time downward adjustment allowed up to 15% with documented forecast variance >25% and 60-day notice; reductions beyond that are subject to pro-rata credits (per the attached clause).
- True-up: 90-day true-up at the end of each 12-month period; monthly refundable credits are limited to 25% of committed monthly run-rate.
- Performance credit: 5% credit available if SLOs missed in months 1–6 (see section 4).

Please review the attached term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_3yr_v1.pdf) and sign the DocuSign envelope here: https://docusign.com/envelopes/3a9f7b. If you want 50/25/25 with 20% discount instead, reply and we'll update the envelope.

If accepted, procurement can expect an invoice within 7 business days of signature (or immediate invoice if 100% upfront selected).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
